value.rationale: Finite experimental landscapes are sample-specific, while the source phenomenology averages rare loss-free regions. The theorem identifies precisely when extreme regions needed by the unrestricted saddle cease to exist in a typical finite sample, creates an explicit sharp crossover, and quantifies a strict polynomial mean-versus-typical gap. For the two physically motivated exponents it discriminates fourth-power from second-power logarithmic time boundaries. The application is a mathematically defined surrogate with an explicit experimentally relevant validity limitation, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputed known mean.
